newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia SKB bank ups div, splits stock.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SKB bank ups div, splits stock.

text.p: Slovenia's second largest bank SKB said on Thursday it would raise its 1996 dividend to 1,300 tolars per share from 1,100 tolars the previous year.
SKB also proposed a stock split whereby each share, currently with a nominal value of 20,000 tolars ($129.4), would be split into 20 new shares with a nominal value of 1,000 tolars each.

The bank said it proposed the stock split in order to make it easier for small shareholders to buy its shares and also to bring the nominal value of shares and global depositary receipts (GDRs) SKBR.MU into line.
In February, SKB became the first Slovenian company to be traded abroad, listing its GDRs on the London, Munich and Frankfurt stock exchanges, with 20 GDRs representing one share.
In March, SKB reported that net profit rose to 1.79 billion tolars from 713 million, while balance sheet assets rose to 208.3 billion tolars from 178.6 billion a year earlier.

On Wednesday shares of SKB listed on the Ljubljana bourse firmed 3.47 percent to 49,150 tolars while its GDRs eased four percent to $35.625. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 153.5 Slovenian Tolars)
